Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a
vote. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
future Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this
meeting. Ask the Secretary if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when
services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or
service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the Planning Commission regarding any item on this agenda after it has been
posted will also be made available for public inspection.

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN (PDP) NO. 2026-01
VESTING TENTATIVE TRACT MAP (VTTM) NO. 85119
CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP) NO. 2026-01
Joe A. Leyva, Global Pacific Investment Co. (“Applicant”); a request to (1) construct a six-
story building consisting of four (4)-stories of 142-unit multi-family residential units
constructed over two (2) levels of podium parking (Proposed Residential Development)
along with associated site improvements; (2) subdivide Parcel “D” of Lot Line Adjustment
No. LLA-20250001 (APN No. 8025-025-010) for condominium purposes, consisting of
142 residential units; and (3) to allow for horizontal mixed-use consisting of the Proposed
Residential Development and an existing six (6) story commercial (office) building on a
6.67±-acre property located at 12501 Imperial Highway (also known as Assessor’s Parcel
Numbers [APNs] 8025-025-008 -009, -010, and -011), within the Professional/Office
(P/O) Zone.
Environmental: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), the project
satisfies all statutory requirements for exemption pursuant to Assembly Bill (AB) 130,
codified at California Public Resources Code Section 21080.66. The Proposed Project is
located on less than 20 acres within an incorporated city, is consistent with both the
General Plan and zoning standards, meets the required density thresholds, and does not
involve any disqualifying environmental conditions or involves the demolition of any listed
historic resources.
The project includes the following applications:
(1) PDP No. 2026-01 – requesting approval to construct a six-story building consisting of
  four (4)-stories of 142-unit multi-family residential units constructed over two (2) levels
  of podium parking, (“Proposed Residential Development”) along with associated site
  improvements; and
(2) VTTM No. 85119 – requesting approval for the subdivision of Parcel “D” of Lot Line
  Adjustment No. LLA-20250001 (APN No. 8025-025-010) for condominium purposes,
  consisting of 142 residential units; and
(3) CUP No. 2026-01 – requesting approval to allow for horizontal mixed-use consisting
  of the Proposed Residential Development and an existing six (6)-story commercial
  (office) building in the Professional/Office (P/O) Zone.

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 3
Minutes of the Adjourned Regular Meeting  September 23, 2026

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Associate Planner Wong
presented a detailed report describing the applicant’s requests to: (1) develop 4-stories
consisting of 142-unit multi-family residential units constructed over two levels of podium
parking (6 stories total), along with associated site improvements on a 6.67±-acre lot at
12501 Imperial Highway; (2) subdivide Parcel “D” of Lot Line Adjustment No. LLA-
20250001 for condominium purposes, consisting of 142 residential units; and (3) allow
for horizontal mixed-use consisting of the proposed residential development and an
existing 6-story commercial office building.

Next, Ms. Wong provided background information on the applicant’s Phase I of the
Norwalk Fitness Village site. She stated that the proposed project is Phase II of a cross-
property development (horizontal mixed use); that the residential floor plans consist of six
distinct plans; that unit sizes will range from 535 square feet to 1,292 square feet; that all
units will feature individual laundry facilities and outdoor balconies; that the proposed third
floor of the building will include amenities and open spaces such as an aqua lounge, pool,
gym, and clubhouse, and that a roof terrace is proposed on the sixth floor.

Continuing with her presentation, Ms. Wong commented on the existing six-story
commercial building stating that the entrance to the building is located along the western
façade; and that the applicant intends to convert a portion of the first-story office area
facing Imperial Highway into restaurant uses in a future phase.

Senior Planner Wong commented on off-street parking and site circulation sharing that
the primary vehicular ingress and egress for the proposed project will be provided by a
30-foot, and 3-inches-wide two-way private driveway along Imperial Highway; that
secondary vehicular ingress and egress will be provided by a 26-foot-wide, two-way
driveway along Imperial Highway, and at a 28-foot-wide, two-way driveway along
Bloomfield Avenue; that the first level of the parking structure will be shared between the
residential and commercial uses; that the second level will be designated for the
residential units; that access to the residential tenants’ parking area will be gated to
provide separation from the commercial uses; that out of the total 593 parking spaces to
be provided, 152 spaces within the parking structure will be assigned spaces for
residential tenants, and the remaining 441 spaces will be shared among residential
visitors, office employees and visitors.

Ms. Wong addressed the General Plan sharing that the project is consistent with the
General Plan designation of Professional Office. She provided a table on the 2021-2029
Housing Element contribution showing “No Net Loss Findings”; and indicated that the
remaining sites identified in the City’ Housing Element are adequate to accommodate the
jurisdiction’s share of the regional housing.

Further, Associate Planner Wong stated that the proposed residential project is in
compliance with the applicable Norwalk Municipal Code Zoning Development Standards;
that the Vesting Tentative Tract Map will comply with the State’s Subdivision Map Act and
all provisions of the City’s Subdivision Ordinance; that the Conditions of Approval require
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 4
Minutes of the Adjourned Regular Meeting  September 23, 2026

the formation of a homeowner’s association (HOA) and the establishment of Covenants,
Conditions and Restrictions (CC&R’s); and that Parkland, Park and Recreation Fees
(“Quimby Act”) pursuant to Norwalk Municipal Code Section 16.03.090 are required; that
Assembly Bill (AB) 130 has been addressed showing that the project satisfies all statutory
requirements for exemption, and that Tribal mitigation measures are included in the draft
Resolution.

In conclusion, Ms. Wong shared that it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning
Commission make the required findings: and (1) Consider and find that the project is
exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act Guidelines pursuant to Assembly
Bill (AB) 130, codified at California Public Resources Code Section 21080.66; and (2)
Adopt Resolution No. 26-15, to approve Precise Development Plan (“PDP”) No. 2026-01,
Vesting Tentative Tract Map (“VTTM”) 85119, and Conditional Use Permit (“CUP”) No.
2026-01 for the Proposed Project subject to Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit
“A”.

The applicant, Joe Leyva, Global Pacific Investment Company, presented testimony. He
stated that their office is located in the office tower at 12501 Imperial Highway, Suite 210;
that they have been at that location since 2016; that they are excited to finally bring their
project to the City in Phases 2 and 3; that, unfortunately, after 2019 when they finished
the center, the market was on a downward trend where they lost about half of their tenants
in the office tower, and most of their retail tenants shut down as well; that in 2024 they
were able to start rebuilding; that they are happy to report that the retail center is one
hundred percent occupied, and the office tower is ninety-five percent occupied; that they
saw an opportunity at the office tower parking lot as it was only used during the week;
that they worked with their consultants to come up with a parking structure; that they have
enough parking for the residents; that the shared parking is sufficient based on actual
number count at ninety-five percent with enough parking for residents, visitors, and
tenants at the office tower site; that this project fits in and provides housing for Norwalk;
that there are five driveways so that there is no danger of traffic issues with coming in or
going out of the site; and that they worked with the City to remove the left turn restriction
going east on Imperial Highway into their office center.

Everado Garcia, LCRA Architecture & Planning, stated that he is part of the team on this
project; that with the subject site they have a unique opportunity where they also have an
employment opportunity, which is not always possible. Mr. Garcia presented a Power
Point presentation of the project site showing the existing commercial uses and office
tower as well as the proposed housing. He stated that they looked at the site to determine
the best location for housing which is towards the center of the site keeping in mind the
residential neighbors to the west; that they have a 154 feet and 6 inches setback from the
property line to the building; that within that area they have landscape buffers which will
help with the visual; that on each side there is a buffer of about 118 feet of separation
between the residential and commercial which also provides some landscaping
opportunities; that, as previously mentioned, there are 142 residential units situated on
top of two levels of residential and shared parking; that on the ground floor they have
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 5
Minutes of the Adjourned Regular Meeting  September 23, 2026

residential uses, amenities, and a parking area; that the second floor is mostly parking
with a small residential lobby; that on the third floor there is a large usable courtyard; that
there is another amenity space on the fourth floor; that the fifth floor is similar to the fourth
floor; that a roof terrace is proposed on the sixth floor; and that they are providing more
open space than required.

The landscape architect, Matt Kohlenberger, Conceptual Design & Planning Company
(CDPC), stated that they were a part of the Phase I team on the Norwalk Fitness Village
project in 2017; that the landscaping throughout the development will feature drought
tolerant plantings, including a diverse mix of trees, including orange trees, shrubs, and
groundcovers; and he explained in detail the landscaping that is going to be provided
throughout the project.

Johnny Lopez stated that he is the owner of Unit No. 18 of the adjacent Silverado Oaks
Townhomes as well as a Board member; that he likes the proposed development;
however, he has a couple of concerns, one being the value of his property and the other
with the noise that will be generated; that, as his wall faces the proposed residential site,
he was glad to hear that they are providing a buffer zone; and that he is excited about the
developments in this community.

Mr. Leyva shared that the City has strict conditions regarding the construction of the
project; that they are always trying to be good neighbors minimizing the effects of the
construction; that they do not anticipate much noise spilling out from the apartments as
everything is centered on the courtyard; that it is a quality project; that his personal opinion
is that it would actually increase the value of the area; and that they would address any
concerns that the neighbors may have.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Apodaca closed
the public testimony.

Commissioner Lopez stated that she likes the modern looking project, and she thanked
staff for their hard work.

Commissioner Macias indicated that it is a well-done project; that the setbacks have been
addressed; that he frequents the busy shopping center; and that he believes that the
parking is going to be a little restricted.

Mr. Leyva stated that with the retail portion, they have about 180 spaces daily that are not
being used; that they are trying to encourage those customers to park on the unused
spaces; and that the parking study shows that only about eighty percent of those parking
spaces are being used at any time.

Commissioner Vernola-Salas shared that staff’s presentation was very informative; that
she is looking forward to the parking lot’s landscaping improvements as well as the
completed project as it will be an asset to the City.

Vice Chair Barragan stated that she agrees with her fellow Commissioners that it is a well
thought out project; that she likes the proposed landscaping while providing some color
with the orange trees; and that she is looking forward to the completed development.

Chair Apodaca shared that the project provides a lot of design elements, including
balconies for every unit, a courtyard and a pool area, and that it is going to be a
spectacular project. Further, she addressed the resident who presented testimony, and
she indicated that they appreciate Mr. Lopez’ input; that construction will be noisy and
that mitigation measures are in place; that once construction is completed, they do not
anticipate a lot of spillover noise as indicated by Mr. Leyva; and that should any concerns

It was moved by Commissioner Vernola-Salas, and seconded by Commissioner Marcias,
to make the required findings and: (1) Consider and find that the project is exempt from

Resolution No. 26-15 to approve Precise Development Plan No. 2026-01, Vesting
Tentative Tract Map No. 85119, and Conditional Use Permit No. 2026-01 for the
Proposed Project subject to Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”.

  Salas, Vice Chair Barragan, and Chair Apodaca

CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT (CUP) NO. 2026-05
Alfredo Lopez (“Applicant”); a request to modify Conditional Use Permit No. 709 by
making the required findings of Public Convenience or Necessity for a California
Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Type 48 (On-Sale General Public
Premises) License in order to reinstate the sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits for
consumption on the premises where sold for a 1,690 square foot bar and billiards
establishment within an existing multi-tenant shopping center located at 10632 Imperial
Highway, (“The Torch Lounge) (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number [APN] 8051-
012-025), within the Restricted Commercial (C-1) Zone.
Conditional Use Permit No. 709 was approved for the operation of a bar and billiards
establishment by the City Council on May 20, 1997 (Resolution No. 4498).
Environmental: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), this
project will not have a significant effect on the environment per Section 15301 (Existing
Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines. Section 15301 consists of the operation involving
negligible expansion of existing use.

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 7
Minutes of the Adjourned Regular Meeting  September 23, 2026

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Assistant Planner Tapia
presented a detailed report on the applicant’s request to modify Conditional Use Permit
No. 709 by making the required findings of Public Convenience or Necessity for a
California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) Type 48 (On-Sale General
Public Premises) License in order to reinstate the sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits
for consumption at The Torch Lounge premises.

Ms. Tapia provided background information on this establishment. She stated that 1978
was the original issue date for the ABC Type 48 license; that on February 26, 1997, the
Planning Commission denied a Conditional Use Permit and Zone Variance request to
establish a bar and billiards operation; that the decision was appealed to the City Council
who approved the request subject to specific operational standards intended to ensure
that alcohol sales remained compatible with surrounding and residential uses; that The
Torch Room ceased operations due to management deficiencies; that Public Safety law
enforcement actions resulted in the revocation of the establishment’s City Business
License in January 2024, which was subsequently followed by the revocation of their ABC
Type 48 license on August 22, 2024.

Continuing with her presentation, Ms. Tapia shared that the applicant, Alfredo Lopez,
purchased the business in 2024 and applied for a new City Business License in December
13, 2024, to operate the billiards establishment, offering soft drinks, snacks and hosting
pool tournaments; that the application was approved for indoor billiards only; that the
business license was not finalized because the tenant space had been declared
substandard by the Building and Safety Division; that the applicant has been working with
City staff to bring the tenant space into compliance; that since the one-year restriction
imposed by ABC has passed, the applicant is now proposing to re-establish the bar and
billiards operation under a new operational plan, and is requestion that the Planning
Commission make the required Public Convenience or Necessity Finding for the transfer
and reinstatement of a Type 48 - On Sale General – Public Premises ABC license, which
is issued to bars and would authorize the sale of beer, wine, and distilled spirits for
consumption on the premises where sold.

Assistant Planner Tapia stated that staff is recommending approval of Conditional Use
Permit No. 2026-05 but is expressing this view with extreme caution due to the manner
of use by the previous owner; and that this recommendation is provided in order to re-
position the use into compliance with applicable laws and requirements of operation.

In response to Commissioner Vernola-Salas’ comment on Condition of Approval No. 27
which requires the applicant to slurry seal the parking surface areas as he is not the
property owner of the site, Deputy City Manager Hamilton stated that he had a
conversation with the applicant about this condition, and that they came to an
understanding that he would take care of the spaces immediately adjacent to his
establishment. Commissioner Vernola-Salas stated that the same condition applies to
the landscaping, and Mr. Hamilton indicated that this is correct.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page No. 8
Minutes of the Adjourned Regular Meeting  September 23, 2026

The applicant, Alfredo Lopez, stated that he has been a Norwalk resident for over forty
years; that his main concern is with safety of his staff and customers; that he is a firm
believer of keeping a clean, safe and friendly bar where customers feel safe and are not
harassed or bothered; that he should not be punished for the previous owner’s operation;
that he is establishing ground rules of customers’ conduct; that he took over Kelley’s
Tavern in Downey a few years ago which has been there for fifty years; that this
community deserves a bar with entertainment where people can go to after work; that
The Torch Lounge is his fourth bar with a Type 48 license; that he is familiar with operating
these types of facilities; that he has a concern with some of the conditions; that he is
allowed to open the establishment at 10:00 a.m. but that he cannot sell alcohol until 11:00
a.m.; that he would like to know what his customers would be doing for an hour; that in
addition, the serving of alcohol is supposed to cease an hour before the 2:00 a.m. closing;
and that a lot of his customers come in late for a drink after work.

In response to Chair Apodaca’s question of the applicant as to the hours he is proposing
for the sale of alcohol, Mr. Lopez indicated that if the facility is really busy on a weekend
he would recommend that the last call be at 1:30 a.m. and that they stop serving alcohol
at 1:40 a.m.; that they have lights that come on at that time to indicate that it is near
closing time, and customers usually leave once those lights come on.

Commissioner Vernola-Salas asked why are the standards being changed for this
applicant. Deputy City Manager Hamilton stated that the conditions imposed were
collaborated on with Public Safety, and that the Commission has the ability to adjust any
conditions. Commissioner Vernola-Salas stated that it seems that the applicant is being
punished for what went on with the previous owner; that they could allow the hours
proposed by the applicant on a trial basis; and that should any problems occur, they could
impose the original conditions.

Lieutenant Noe Garcia stated that he and the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department,
Norwalk Station, are opposed to allowing the applicant to open this facility; that it took a
lot of time and effort to have the bar closed; that there was at least a two-year undercover
operation between the Sheriff’s Department and the Department of Alcoholic Beverage
Control; that once the bar was closed, crime in the area dropped; that the bar had been
taken over by gangs and motorcycle gangs; that, in his opinion, the neighborhood does
not lend itself for such a facility; that a lot of resources have been spent on responding to
calls for service to that bar; that he does not believe that the neighbors in that area are
aware that the bar is trying to re-open; that, he, too, was not asked to comment on the
applicant’s request; and that he is representing his Department as well as the City with
his comments.

Mr. Lopez stated that he completely agrees with the comments made by Lieutenant
Garcia regarding the bar’s previous operation; and that he does not allow gangs to
frequent any of his facilities.

disposal and glass dumping into exterior bins shall be prohibited between the hours of
9:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. to minimize noise impacts on surrounding properties.

Mr. Lopez shared that they have an older lady come by in the daytime to pick up bottles;
that at his other places that are close to residences he displays signage that says not to
open that door between certain hours and to not make noise.

Introduction/background:

California has enacted numerous housing laws intended to streamline and provide greater
predictability in local approval processes for certain housing development projects. The Housing
Accountability Act (Government Code Section 65589.5) generally prohibits cities and counties
from denying a housing development project or reducing its density based on a subjective design
standard. Applicable projects must be reviewed against “objective, quantifiable, written
development standards, conditions, and policies” and may only be denied if certain findings
specified in Government Code Section 65589.5(j) are met. State housing law defines an
“objective design standard” as a standard that “involves no personal or subjective judgment by a
public official and is uniformly verifiable by reference to an external and uniform benchmark or
criterion available and knowable by both the development applicant or proponent and the public
official before submittal of an application” (Gov. Code §66300(a)(7)).

In compliance with State housing law, the City of Norwalk 6th Cycle Housing Element Update
(HEU), recertified by the Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) on
September 19, 2025, includes Program 3.3 Objective Design Standards. Program 3.3 commits
the City to establish objective design standards for applicable residential development consistent
with State housing law.

Program 3.3 provides for the establishment of objective design standards to facilitate local
guidance on the design and standards for by-right projects as allowed by State law, and to
facilitate high-quality residential development consistent with State housing objectives. The
Program identifies private open space, parking, and related features, as well as architectural
design.

On June 28, 2026, HCD sent the City a letter inquiring about the status of the City’s 6th Cycle
Housing Element implementation programs pursuant to Government Code section 65585(i). The
letter identified outstanding implementation items and requested information regarding the City’s
progress in completing the identified programs, including Program 3.3, Objective Design
Standards.

On July 16, 2026, the City submitted a response to HCD addressing each of its concerns,
including Program 3.3, and communicated that the adoption of the objective design standards
was anticipated prior to November 1, 2026. The proposed Zoning Text Amendment would
establish the objective design standards identified in Program 3.3 and represents the City’s action
toward completing implementation of the program.

Zoning Text Amendment No. 2026-03:

The City’s existing Zoning Code contains development standards that regulate residential
projects according to their zoning district and type of development. These regulations address
matters such as setbacks, building height, lot coverage, density, open space, landscaping,
architectural and building design, off-street parking, wall and fence heights, and signage. Zoning
Text Amendment (ZTA) No. 2026-01 builds upon this existing regulatory framework by
establishing objective design standards specifically for qualifying attached multi-family and
townhome residential development.

The proposed ZTA would add Article V – Objective Design Standards - Sections 17.03.400
through 17.03.470 to Title 17 (Zoning) of the NMC to establish objective design standards for
new qualifying attached multi-family and townhome residential developments. The proposed
standards are intended to provide clear, measurable, and enforceable requirements, while
achieving and maintaining high-quality site planning and building design consistent with the City’s
community design priorities. The proposed objective design standards are also influenced by the
design criteria in the Heart of Norwalk Specific Plan, which went through robust community
outreach prior to adoption.

Sections 17.03.400 through 17.03.430 would establish objective design standards for attached
multi-family development addressing the principal elements of site and building design, including
building orientation, pedestrian access and accommodations, parking layout, site circulation,
building massing and articulation, architectural features, materials and colors, building entries
and windows, roof design and screening, fences and walls, and lighting. Sections 17.03.440
through 17.03.470 would establish separate standards for residential townhome development
addressing comparable site and building design considerations, with standards tailored to
townhome development.

The proposed standards would supplement and be in addition to the development standards of
the applicable zoning district. They would not replace the underlying zoning district requirements.
In the event of a conflict with other provisions in Title 17, the new objective design standards
would govern.

The standards would apply to new qualifying residential development where State law limits the
City’s enforcement of design standards to objective standards or where State law or the Municipal
Code requires a ministerial approval process. The proposed provisions exclude non-qualifying
single-family homes, non-qualifying multi-family properties, historic properties, and any non-
residential developments. Mixed-use projects would continue to be regulated under Article VI of
Title 17.

Overall, the proposed amendment would establish objective design standards for key site and
building design elements of qualifying attached multi-family and townhome residential
development. The standards would provide measurable criteria for the review of applicable

Ordinance failed to comply with State ADU laws.

  the Ordinance that explain the reasons the City believes that the Ordinance complies with
  State ADU Law despite HCD’s findings.

General that the City is in violation of State ADU Law. As such, City staff opted to proceed
with item no. 1 listed above.

   § 17.04.210. Accessory dwelling units and junior accessory dwelling units.
  A.  Purpose. The purpose of this section is to establish regulations governing accessory
  dwelling units (ADUs) and junior accessory dwelling Units (JADUs) in accordance
  with California Government Code Section66310 through 66342, et seq., as amended
  from time to time, and other applicable state laws. This section is not intended to
  conflict with State law and shall be interpreted to be compatible with state
  enactments. Facilitating the development of ADUs and JADUs will increase the
  availability of affordable housing to suit the variety of lifestyles and needs of the
  community, while mitigating impacts on traffic, utilities, and public health and
  safety and preserving the character of residential neighborhoods.
  B.  Definitions. Words and terms as used in ADU and JADU regulations of this section
  are defined as follows:
  "Accessory Building" or "Accessory Structure" means a detached structure that is
  accessory and incidental to a dwelling located on the same lot.
  "Accessory Dwelling Unit" or "ADU" means an attached or detached residential
  unit that provides complete independent living facilities for one or more persons and
  is located on a lot with a proposed or existing primary residential unit. It shall
  include permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation
  and be located on the same parcel that the primary residential unit is or will be
  situated. An accessory dwelling unit can also be an efficiency unit, as defined in
  Cal. Health & Safety Code § 17958.1 or a manufactured home, as defined in Cal.
  Health & Safety Code § 18007.
  "Attached" means the ADU or Junior ADU shares a wall with the existing or
  proposed single dwelling or the multiple-family dwelling, with both sides of the wall
  being habitable space. ADUs or Junior ADUs shall not be connected to the existing
  or proposed single-family dwelling or multiple-family structure solely by a patio
  cover, breezeway or similar roofed area.
  "Building Height" means height is measured at existing legal grade to the peak of
  the structure.
  "Complete Independent Living Facilities" means permanent provisions for living,
  sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation on the same parcel as the single-family or
  multiple-family dwelling is or will be situated.
  "Detached" means the ADU is physically separated from the existing or proposed
  single dwelling or the multiple-family dwelling.
  "Efficiency Dwelling Unit" means a dwelling unit which contains a minimum of
  150 square feet in living space, a separate closet, kitchen sink, cooking appliance,
  refrigerator, and a separate bathroom containing a water closet, lavatory, bathtub, or
  shower.
  "Efficiency Kitchen" means a kitchen that includes at a minimum:
  1.  Appliances for cooking food and refrigeration, either built-in or countertop.

  prior to approval. For the purposes of this definition, enclosed uses are within the
  residence, with the exception of attached garages, to be a part of the proposed or
  existing single-family residence and enclosed with solid walls on a minimum of
  three sides.

   § 17.04.400. Density bonus.
  A.  Purpose. It is the purpose of this section to encourage the production of very low-,
  low-, and moderate-income housing units, senior citizens housing units, provisions
  of childcare facilities, student housing units, special needs housing units, and
  donations of land in accordance with Government Code Sections 65915 through
  65918, as may be amended from time to time ("State Density Bonus Law"). In
  enacting this section, it is also the intent of the City to facilitate the development of
  affordable housing and to implement the goals, objectives, and policies of the
  housing element of the City's General Plan, including Program 2.1 (Special Needs
  Housing).
  B.  Definitions. Whenever the following terms are used in this section, they shall have
  the meaning established:
  "Affordable rent" as defined in Health and Safety Code Section 50053(b).
  "Affordable sales price" means a sales price at which very low-, low-, or moderate-
  income households can qualify for the purchase of target units, calculated in
  accordance with Health and Safety Code Section 50052.5 and the regulations
  adopted by the California Department of Housing and Community Development.
  "Base density" means the maximum allowable gross residential density permitted
  under this Title and the Land Use Element of the General Plan or any specific plan
  applicable to the proposed development, as of the date of application submittal by
  the applicant to the City. If the underlying zoning district is inconsistent with the
  base density allowed under the Land Use Element of the General Plan, the greater
  shall prevail.
  "Base project" means the proposed housing development before any extra density
  is added through the State Density Bonus Law in accordance with all local
  regulations, without including any bonus units, concessions, or waivers.
  "Base unit" means only those units permitted by the underlying zoning regulations,
  excluding any units added through a density bonus awarded pursuant to this section
  or any other provisions of the Norwalk Municipal Code granting a greater density
  bonus.
  "Commercial project" means a development that includes commercial uses like
  retail, office, or industrial spaces, and may also apply to mixed-use developments.
  "Concession" shall have the same meaning as the term "incentive" defined herein.
  "Density bonus" means a density increase of up to those percentages specified in the
  State Density Bonus Law above the otherwise maximum residential density under
